text: ユメを　たべるという　でんせつの　いきもの　バクの　しそん。
note: The baku is a creature of Japanese folklore, originally from China, that devours nightmares; people traditionally called on it to eat a bad dream. The same word バク also means the tapir, the real animal.
claim: In Japanese folklore the baku is a supernatural creature that eats dreams and nightmares, and the same word is used for the tapir.

check.quote: Japanese supernatural beings that are said to devour nightmares. They originate from the Chinese Mo. … The Japanese term baku has two current meanings, referring to both the traditional dream-devouring creature and to the Malayan tapir. … A child having a nightmare in Japan will wake up and repeat three times, 'Baku-san, come eat my dream.'
